requirement:
No prompt, tool result, or tool error the harness gives the model MUST state a
line number or line range of a project source, except within source text it
quotes and where a tool error repeats a line number the model supplied. The
harness MUST identify a source location by file and outline selector under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors` instead.
rationale:
The requirement is mostly met, but one tool-error path still gives the model line numbers it did not supply, so I judge it unmet.

**What is covered**
- **Tool results.**
  - `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[outline_entries]` gives the selector, kind and name of each outline node, with no line numbers.
  - `src/authoring/tools.rs#impl[SearchNodes]/fn[entries]` gives file, selector, kind and text lines with an elision marker, with no line numbers.
  - `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[references]` gives file and selector only.
  - `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[to_model_input]` gives the file, selector, hash, kind and text of each input.
  - `src/sites.rs#impl[SiteItem]/fn[matches_value]` gives selectors for site matches.
  - Tests in `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]` assert that results carry no `line_start`, `line_end` or `line` fields. Examples are `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms`, `search_merges_context_windows_and_respects_ignore_rules` and `outline_lists_nested_nodes_without_text_or_inputs`.
- **Tool errors that repeat the model's own numbers.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[read_lines]` repeats only the line numbers the model supplied. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tool_errors_give_the_model_no_line_numbers_it_did_not_supply]` tests this.
- **Source parse errors.** `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#fn[without_source_lines]` strips `line N: ` from parse errors. `converse` in `src/authoring/mod.rs` applies it to every tool error. `tool_errors_drop_the_source_line_of_a_parse_error` and the `mod.rs` test above exercise it.
- **Location by file and selector.** The code above gives locations as file plus selector.

**Gap: some tool errors state project-source line numbers the model did not supply**
- The `ast_grep` tool's `{query}` form (`src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[declared_query]`) calls `crate::structural::declared_queries`. That function returns the first problem from `src/structural.rs#fn[parse_queries]`.
- Those problems are formatted as `"{file}:{line}: query {name} is not closed"`, `"{file}:{line}: query {name} must contain exactly one fenced yaml code block"`, and `"{file}:{line}: query {name}: the yaml block must be a mapping ...: {error}"`. They give the line of a project chapter file (for example `md/requirements.md`), and the YAML decoder's own message may add more.
- `declared_query` returns that string unchanged as an `io::Error`. `converse` then runs it through `without_source_lines`, whose pattern `\bline \d+: ` does not match `file:LINE:`. The model therefore receives a project-source line number it did not supply.
- Nothing carries an `{impl}` reference for this path, and no test covers it. The existing tests only exercise `read_lines` and parse errors of the form `line N: `.
- The requirement says "No … tool error … MUST state a line number or line range of a project source", so this is a violation of its text, not an edge case it leaves open.
- The reference-discovery error aggregation in `fn[references]` and `declared_query` could carry the same kind of message. I did not trace whether it does.

No `{fixme}` acknowledges this gap.

**Smaller point**
- `converse` in `src/authoring/mod.rs` is the code that applies the line-number filter to every tool error, but it carries no `{impl}` reference to this requirement.

text: No prompt, tool result, or tool error the harness gives the model MUST state a
line number or line range of a project source, except within source text it
quotes and where a tool error repeats a line number the model supplied. The
harness MUST identify a source location by file and outline selector under
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
